cost_note: Published per-image rate for one Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image 1K output. The Gemini Developer API generateContent response carries no per-call invoiced dollar amount, so measured spend is (successful images x published per-image rate) — the same basis every prior Gemini receipt in this repo uses. Token usage per call is recorded in usage_metadata as corroborating evidence. A blocked/safety-filtered image is not charged (confirmed by the provider's own error message) and is excluded from total_cost_usd.

Scene / background: The interior of a small independent barbershop on a weekday afternoon. Three stations along one mirrored wall, each with its own warm practical bulb; the rest of the room falls away into a low plum-dark. The shop is plainly working - clippings on the tiled floor, capes hung, two chairs occupied.
Subject: In the upper third of the frame, one empty barber's chair turned three-quarters toward camera: cracked leather honestly worn through at the seat edge, a folded cape over the arm, a set of clippers laid down on the station shelf beside it. Behind it, softly out of focus, the shop's owner - a Black man in his late thirties, deep brown skin, close fade and a short trimmed beard, plain dark work shirt - stands at the next station mid-cut, hands working, absorbed and completely in command of what he is doing. Further back at the third chair, a second barber with pale freckled skin and an auburn beard leans in over his own client, equally absorbed.
Key details: Hair clippings underfoot, a comb standing in a jar, a towel over a shoulder, fingerprints on the mirror, a scuffed chrome footrest, a worn spray bottle. Every object is used and cared for. Nothing is new, nothing is styled, nobody is posing for the camera. The bottom 40 percent of the frame is empty tiled floor receding into shadow.
Camera and light: 35mm at seat height, very slight low angle, shallow depth of field holding the empty chair sharp while the working barbers fall soft behind it.
Photograph it, do not illustrate it: real optics, natural depth of field, one dominant light source, visible film grain, and honest material wear — scuffs, dust, fingerprints, faded paint, worn edges, uneven surfaces. Ordinary and unstaged, as if caught in the moment on a working day. Do not render it as 8K, ultra-detailed, hyper-real, studio-polished, cinematic, or heavily retouched.

campaign_spend_correction.why: total_cost_usd counts KEPT images only. generate-plates.mjs merges results by id, so a retake overwrites the first take's row and its cost disappears from the total. Three plates were regenerated after visual review (bl-01-square-1x1, bl-04-story-9x16, bl-05-square-1x1), so the receipt shows 12 where 15 successful generations were actually billed.
campaign_spend_correction.discard_reason: First takes rendered the reserved negative space as a flat pasted panel with a hard seam, and one arrived with a white polaroid border - both explicitly excluded by the prompt. Caught by looking at the images, not by any tool status.
campaign_spend_correction.basis: 15 successful generations x $0.0336 published per-image rate for one Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image 1K output. The generateContent response carries no invoiced dollar amount; this is the same basis every Gemini receipt in this repo uses.
campaign_spend_correction.other_paid_providers_used: none - Photoshop compositing is $0 on the existing Adobe subscription, and no HeyGen, OpenAI, MuAPI or Firefly call was made.
